title: private-installer: automate TLS + KMS rotation with Vault + sealed-secrets and upgrade hooks
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: automate certificate and KMS key rotations for Private Installer deployments (VPC/on-prem) to reduce manual ops, avoid expired cert incidents, and integrate with Vault/KMS-backed HSMs. This PR implements a coordinated rotation flow: (1) Terraform changes to create/rotate cloud KMS keys (with aliases and IAM bindings for installer service accounts), (2) Helm chart updates to expose rotation hooks and sidecar for sealed-secrets reconciliation, (3) installer post-upgrade hooks that trigger Vault CSR issuance and distribute new TLS certs via sealed-secrets, and (4) rollback-safe sequencing with health checks and traffic-draining steps. Includes additional docs and an upgrade playbook.

What changed: consolidated into four areas: terraform modules, helm charts, installer runtime hooks, and ops scripts. Key design points: - Rotation is performed as a multi-step, idempotent state machine (rotate-kms -> issue-csr -> seal-secret -> deploy -> validate). - Sealed-secrets remains the distribution mechanism for certs to avoid storing plaintext in git; Vault is the CA/secret source. - We add an opt-in flag in values.yaml to enable automatic rotations and a dry-run mode for testing. - Rollback uses previous sealed-secret revision with a forced rekey path in case HSM key schedule fails.

Checklist (manual and automated): [x] Terraform plan and apply tested in staging; [x] Helm lint and install tested against kind cluster; [x] E2E rotation smoke test (staging) passes; [x] Security review of Vault policies; [x] Upgrade/rollback playbook added.

Upgrade notes: to enable automatic rotation set values.autoRotation.enabled=true and provide vault config (address, role, token/K8s auth). For on-prem air-gapped installs, operator must provide Vault reachable endpoint or configure an offline CSR signing flow using HSM signing appliance (see docs/installer/rotation/offline.md). Backward compatibility: default remains manual rotation; no secret access changes unless flag enabled.

Rollback plan: installer records previous sealed-secret revisions in installer-state ConfigMap. On failure, operator can run ./scripts/rollback-rotation --revision <n>. The PR includes a health-check that waits for webhook and TLS handshake validation before marking rotation complete.

Security considerations: Vault role limited to PKI/sign only; Terraform KMS key grants constrained to installer service account; sealed-secrets controller access limited via namespace RBAC. We add audit annotations and KMS key alias rotation logs to CloudWatch/Stackdriver.

Follow-ups: add automated rotation dashboards in observability-pack and a Linera ticket to run scheduled rotations for dedicated customers. Linked Linear/alerts included below.

chore(terraform): add kms_key module with rotation alias and iam bindings
feat(helm): expose rotation.enabled and dryRun flags, sidecar for sealed-secrets reconciliation
docs: add upgrade playbook, offline signing guide
test: e2e rotation smoke test and fixture updates
fix: handle sealed-secrets version skew during rollout
diff_snippets:
+ values.yaml: rotation:
    enabled: false # opt-in
    dryRun: true # don't commit secrets when true
+ charts/templates/hooks/rotate-job.yaml: added post-install Job that runs ./post-rotate.sh and waits for validation status
+ installer/hooks/post-rotate.sh: invokes vault pki/issue, kubectl create secret sealedsecret --from-file=crt.pem and marks rotation success in ConfigMap
review_comments: Ethan Cole: Can we avoid granting kms:CreateAlias to the installer SA? Suggest Terraform create alias and give only encrypt/decrypt to installer.
Priya Shah: Updated Terraform to create alias during provisioning; installer agent only needs generate/data key permissions (see terraform/modules/kms/main.tf commit).
Marta Novak: Helm values look good but add integration test coverage for sealed-secrets version skew.
Priya Shah: Added e2e fixture that simulates sealed-secrets controller restart during rollout and validated reconciliation path.
Diego Morales: How do we ensure Vault auth token isn't leaked in CI logs?
Priya Shah: CI uses vault-agent with Kubernetes auth and tokens are injected via ephemeral pods; updated ci/e2e-rotation.yaml to redact logs and use k8s secrets mounted as files.
release_notes:
- Added automated TLS and KMS rotation flow for Private Installer (opt-in).
- Terraform module for KMS key creation with rotation and required IAM bindings.
- Helm hooks and installer scripts to issue CSRs via Vault and distribute certs using sealed-secrets.
- New upgrade/rollback playbook and e2e rotation smoke tests.
notes_for_oncall: If customers enable auto-rotation and Vault becomes unavailable, rotation jobs will retry and will not overwrite active certs. Monitor rotation_failure_count metric and sealed-secrets reconciliation metrics. Rollback can be triggered with scripts/rotation/rollback-rotation.
